results.correct_value: 5.8 with some A1 aid (5.8/A1), possible to lead free; no free grade of 5.9 is published
results.evidence: The route page lists South Face at 5.8/A1, Grade III-IV, 7 pitches, 'originally done with some aid, possible to lead free'. The 1969 first-ascent account rates the free climbing F5-F8 (hardest F8 = 5.8) with the curving chimney climbed on aid. Neither gives a free grade of 5.9; the 5.9 figures were unsourced.

patches.find: a classic mixed free/aid granite climb, now commonly led free in the 5.8-5.9 range.
patches.replace: a classic granite climb at 5.8 with some original A1 aid, which can be led free.

results.correct_value: about 23 miles from Winthrop to the Andrews Creek Trailhead
results.evidence: One Pasayten guide says the road is paved for 23.5 miles to the Andrews Creek Trailhead; another says drive 23 miles up the Chewuch River road to the Andrews Creek trail. The Forest Service text ('6 miles ... then 22 miles') is ambiguous and was read as 28; the straight-line distance Winthrop to trailhead is about 21 miles along a fairly straight valley, consistent with ~23. Sibling Monk/NE Ridge rows still say 28 miles consistently (not patched here; same class).

patches.find: ~6 miles on Okanogan County Rd 1213/West Chewuch Rd from Winthrop, then ~22 miles on Forest Road 51 to the trailhead
patches.replace: about 23 miles from Winthrop, the first ~6 on Okanogan County Rd 1213/West Chewuch Rd and the rest on Forest Road 51 to the trailhead

patches.find: then continue ~22 paved miles to the trailhead
patches.replace: then continue on pavement to the trailhead, about 23 miles from Winthrop in all

results.correct_value: 3rd-class scramble whose crux is a Class 4 step across the summit gap
results.evidence: Two route descriptions rate the summit gap crossing Class 4 ('cross the gap (Class 4)'), and scramble summaries describe Class 3 to near the summit with a Class 4 crux move; the peak's easiest line is rated class 3 overall. The row's own Southwest Route (the same terrain) says 'Class 3 with one Class 4 step-across'. The TIME part stays open: one 2024 trip report took 1h10m summit to camp, fitting the prose's '45 min to just over an hour' but not the schedule's 1.5-2.5 h; a second summit-to-camp time is needed to settle the schedule.

results.evidence: Split out from 'Descent grade and time': the prose says about 45 min to just over an hour summit to camp; the day-2 schedule allows 4:00 PM to 5:30-6:30 PM. One 2024 trip report gives 1h10m summit to camp; no second source found. A second published summit-to-camp time would settle it.

results.correct_value: snow typically clears the approach and route by early July
results.evidence: A 2024 trip report (June 30-July 6) found the snow almost entirely gone as June ends and the ice axes and microspikes unnecessary. A 2016 conditions thread reports the route itself snow-free by late May with the approach and descent clearing through June in hot weather. Both support early July, not mid-July.

patches.find: Snow typically clears from the route and approach by mid-July
patches.replace: Snow typically clears from the route and approach by early July

results.evidence: The route page gives only 'wide range of nuts/cams'; a photo caption calls the last pitch a 4-inch splitter. No source found for doubles to #3 plus a #4, nor for a single set to 3 in. Settled by a published rack for this route.

One source (a photo caption on the route page: 'Final 4" splitter ... amazing rock quality') supports the pitch table's ~4-inch crack against the overview's hand/finger; the description says only 'jam crack'. No second independent source found; the row has only two fields on each side, too few for the internal rule.

The route is 1-2 pitches low on the tower's south face; no source gives the elevation of the route's top or of The Monk's top, so neither high_point_ft (8,606, Cathedral's summit) nor the 8,300-ft topout pin can be corrected from research. Settled by a sourced elevation for the base/top of the West Cracks or the Monk.

results.correct_value: Class 3 route with one Class 4 step-across at the summit chasm
results.evidence: Two route descriptions rate the gap crossing just below the summit Class 4, and the peak's standard line is rated class 3 overall. The beta's closing sentence muddled the two; it now states the route is Class 3 with the one Class 4 move, matching rock_grade and the pitch table.

patches.find: It is Class 3 with exposure that makes it Class 4-.
patches.replace: Overall the route is Class 3, with that one Class 4 move at the chasm and exposure well beyond the grade.

results.correct_value: starts on the open South Face left of the Cathedral-Monk gully, between the central (Beckey) line and the Doorish route
results.evidence: The first-ascent report says the route begins between the Beckey and Doorish routes on the highly featured face, crosses the Beckey ramp to a headwall crack and finishes on the Southeast Buttress's last pitch. The Southeast Buttress description places that route on the ridge behind The Monk, i.e. in the Cathedral-Monk gully, so the gully is not this route's start.

patches.find: then into the Cathedral-Monk gully to the base of the South Face.
patches.replace: then toward the Cathedral-Monk gully and along the base to its left, to the open South Face.
